idea: Book on the generalist research method
buyer: Professionals wanting to think and research better
pain: No good book on how a generalist gets to a defensible view quickly
v1: A proposal and three sample chapters
verdict: A credibility asset rather than a business; judge it as marketing for the advisory work.

why.distribution: A publisher provides some distribution; she has no platform to drive sales herself.
why.demand: Inferred; business books sell poorly unless the author already has an audience.
why.fmf: Her method is genuinely distinctive and she can write - the content would be good.
why.revenue_structure: An advance then royalties, essentially one-off.
why.defensibility: A book is a durable credibility asset that keeps working for years.
why.ceiling: A typical advance is £5-15k and most books never earn out.

ceiling_arithmetic: A first-time business book advance is typically £5-15k, paid in instalments over two years, with most never earning royalties beyond it. As a year-one business: essentially zero.
carries: A durable credibility asset that would raise her price on every advisory idea in this list.
kills: Time to revenue of two years and an advance that is a rounding error. It is not a business.
test: Write the proposal and test it on two agents.
test_fail: They ask what her platform is - the standard first question.
